claims.claim: Mosaic sits in a food-system causal chain where crop yields require nutrient replacement, linking mined/processed phosphate and potash to agricultural productivity and human food needs; this gives the products structural utility but not immunity from commodity cycles.

The Brazil curtailment demonstrates a successor bottleneck: essential end demand can coexist with uneconomic conversion when sulfur/input costs rise enough, shifting constraint from nutrient need to feedstock economics and plant utilization.

factors.name: alignment2036
factors.basis: Phosphate and potash replenish crop nutrients that support agricultural output.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Mosaic controls meaningful nutrient production assets, but sulfur/input economics can become the binding constraint.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Food production need is durable while fertilizer affordability, crop economics and input costs remain cyclical.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Farmers can optimize rates and nutrient sources, but phosphorus and potassium requirements cannot be eliminated indefinitely without yield/soil tradeoffs.

risks.risk: Input-cost inflation can make nutrient production uneconomic even when end-market need remains intact.

causalEdges.from: crop nutrient depletion and food demand
causalEdges.mechanism: harvested crops remove nutrients that must be replenished to sustain productive yields
causalEdges.falsifier: agronomic substitution or efficiency materially reduces required purchased nutrient intensity without yield loss

causalEdges.mechanism: higher conversion costs can push production below acceptable margins and trigger curtailment
causalEdges.falsifier: pricing, process efficiency or input normalization restores durable economic utilization

unknowns.unknown: Current fertilizer pricing, realized volumes and post-curtailment economics are not established by the reused evidence.

claims.claim: Essentiality of crop nutrients should not be conflated with pricing power or asset profitability; the documented Brazil curtailment is direct evidence that input-cost shocks can overpower end-demand utility at the plant level.
The dividend is evidence of a capital return decision, not evidence that curtailed phosphate economics have normalized.

factors.name: inputCostExposure
factors.basis: Sulfur inflation was severe enough to extend production curtailments.

factors.name: commodityCyclicality
factors.basis: Nutrient need persists, but realized margins depend on fertilizer prices, crop economics, supply response and feedstock costs.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Product essentiality and a dividend should not be extrapolated into durable margin resilience.

risks.risk: Persistent sulfur/input inflation can keep capacity curtailed or compress margins after restart.
Commodity supply response and farmer affordability can weaken realized pricing despite long-run nutrient need.

causalEdges.mechanism: variable cost can exceed economic production threshold
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained restart at acceptable margins despite elevated input costs

contradictions.claim: Structurally essential products versus curtailed production
contradictions.resolution: Resolved as an economics distinction: essential end use does not guarantee every production route is profitable at every input-price point.

unknowns.unknown: Evidence does not establish current restart status or full-quarter profitability.
